newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products edge down on weaker crude.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products edge down on weaker crude.

text.p: Singapore oil products prices edged down in quiet trading on weaker crude values with jet fuel talked firmer on renewed winter buying, traders said on Monday.
Traders added that the unexpected shutdown of a 100,000-bpd crude unit in north Taiwan may lead to some jet fuel purchases.

Also recent purchases from Japan and China has led to stronger premiums in Singapore with a 30,000-tonne cargo sold for mid-December lifting at a 10-cent premium to Singapore spot quotes, on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
Japan and China had last week bought four spot cargoes for arrival in December, traders said.
Gas oil swaps fell on lower crude with December traded at $30.00 and $29.95. down from Friday's $30.10/$30.20 close. The Dec/Jan backwardation narrowed by 10 cents to 40/50 cents.

Traders said market remained balanced with no new cargoes seen headed to the region from the west as the arbitrage was now closed. As a result, premiums in Singapore and the Middle East should improve, they added.

Two 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil cargoes were sold last week before the arbitrage closed at 30 cents premium to MidEast quoted on a free-on-board basis, down about 20-30 cents from the previous deal, traders said.
Fuel oil traded down $1 from Friday with 20,000 tonnes done at $118 a tonne between a major and a local trader, fob.

Naphtha edged down with crude but traders still said prices were being well-supported by demand in north Asia. Majors in Singapore were heard shipping their own system barrels to affiliates in Japan and two shosha covered short-requirements at firm prices. Premiums were assessed at around 60 cents a barrel over Singapore quotes.
A 95-octane gasoline cargo traded at $25.75 a barrel between a Singapore trader a Japanese trader.
